sections.html:
Woodstock is the McHenry County seat, about 51 miles northwest of Chicago, and most owners who sell are moving closer to work, downsizing, settling an estate or leaving a rental behind. The town square, the Opera House and the old county courthouse anchor a historic district, which draws buyers who like older homes.

That mix of older homes near downtown and newer subdivisions on the edges means two very different sales. A century-old house near the square may call for a roof or rewiring, while a newer one farther out tends to sell on location and school boundaries.

Woodstock has about 10,650 households, and nearly three in ten of them rent. Population was 25,630 at the 2020 count and is estimated at 25,740 for 2025.

Woodstock Community Unit School District 200 serves the city. For many buyers, the school buildings and the train station matter as much as the house.

  • District 200 runs an early learning center (Verda Dierzen) and six elementary schools: Dean Street, Greenwood, Mary Endres, Olson, Prairiewood and Westwood.
  • Two middle schools, Northwood and Creekside, feed Woodstock High School and Woodstock North High School.
  • St. Mary Catholic grade school covers kindergarten through eighth grade in town, and many students go on to Marian Central Catholic High School.
  • Woodstock station is on Metra's Union Pacific Northwest Line, the second to last stop before Harvard, with 14 weekday trains to Chicago.

Name the train line and the school district in any listing. Cash buyers weigh the same things, plus the repair list.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in McHenry County
sections.html:
The deed is recorded with the McHenry County Recorder, and a transfer declaration (PTAX-203 or the online MyDec) has to accompany it. A document that meets state requirements and comes with the right fee is recorded the same day it is received, and documents usually come back within about two working days. Call 815-334-4110 for fee questions.

One point helps sellers here: no municipality in McHenry County charges a separate transfer tax. So the Woodstock closing does not add a city stamp like those in some other Illinois towns. The state still expects a signed declaration to travel with every deed (35 ILCS 200/31-25).

Before closing, search for liens. The Recorder will help you look for liens and foreclosures filed against a property. The County Treasurer (815-334-4072) and County Clerk (815-334-4242) handle questions on unpaid taxes and property sold for back taxes. The Assessor's office at 815-334-4290 can confirm who owns a parcel.

If taxes or a lien turn up, the amount is paid from your proceeds at closing and the deed passes clear. Call these offices early so the figure you hear is current, and ask for it in writing.

Open or missing permits show up in a buyer's inspection. Woodstock's Building and Planning staff issue permits for work such as roofs, furnaces, water heaters, decks, fences, garages, sheds, solar panels, plumbing and electrical work, and for windows or doors when the opening changes size. Driveways and aprons need zoning approval only.

  • Express permits are generally issued in 3 to 5 business days, and typical review for other projects is 10 to 15 business days.
  • Most building permits last 120 days, while a permit for a new principal building or an addition lasts 12 months, with a written extension possible for good cause.
  • A final inspection is required before a building is used or occupied, and inspections need at least 48 hours' notice at 815-338-4305.

If an earlier owner finished the basement or added a deck without a permit, speak with Building and Planning before you list. A cash purchaser may overlook it, but a lender's appraiser might not.

Title 4, Chapter 13 of the Woodstock City Code sets up a performance-based Property Management Program. An owner who is found liable for two or more code violations in one rental unit within six months must register every unit they own, at no fee, and return the form within 30 days. An owner found liable for four or more violations in a single unit within 12 months needs a city permit to keep renting.

That permit depends on interior and exterior inspections. The unit that triggered it is inspected, and so are all of an owner's units if they own eight or fewer in the city. For larger owners the city inspects the original unit plus up to 25% of the rest. The first inspection and re-inspection are free, and a third and later ones cost $40 each. The requirement ends after twelve months without another finding of liability.

If you are selling a rental, ask Building and Planning whether the property is under the program. An investor who buys it will want to know before offering.

A quick sale is realistic when the house is priced to match the repairs it needs and the paperwork is clean. You have three paths, and the right one depends on condition and timing.

  • Agent listing: you wait on showings, an appraisal and the buyer's financing. It suits a sound house near the Square.
  • Owner sale: no commission, though the contract, disclosure and showings land on you.
  • Cash purchase: no financing step and few repair requests. It fits estate houses, tenant-occupied homes and houses with code violations.

Get any offer in writing and compare the net after repairs, taxes and carrying cost.

Whichever route you take, the steps after you accept an offer look alike. A title company searches the record for liens, you request a payoff letter from any lender, and the seller disclosure report goes to the buyer before the contract is signed. At closing you sign the deed, the proceeds come to you, and the McHenry County Recorder files the deed with its PTAX-203 declaration. A cash buyer skips the loan approval and the appraisal, so the schedule follows the title work and your move date.

faqs.q: Does the City of Woodstock charge its own transfer tax?
faqs.a: No. No municipality in McHenry County charges a separate transfer tax. You still file a transfer declaration (PTAX-203 or MyDec) with the deed, and the recorder's fees apply.

faqs.q: Which office records a Woodstock deed?
faqs.a: Record it with the McHenry County Recorder. Call 815-334-4110 with fee questions. Documents that meet state requirements and have the correct fee are recorded the same day they are received.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed for a new roof or furnace in Woodstock?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's permit list includes roofs, furnace installs or replacements, water heaters, fences, decks and sheds. Express permits generally take 3 to 5 business days, so apply early if you want the work finished before listing.

faqs.q: What if my Woodstock rental has had code violations?
faqs.a: Registration becomes mandatory after two or more violations in one unit within six months, and a permit with inspections is required after four or more within 12 months. Registration is free, and the first inspection and re-inspection carry no charge.

faqs.q: Who can tell me whether property taxes are owed on a Woodstock parcel?
faqs.a: Ask the McHenry County Treasurer at 815-334-4072 about unpaid tax and the County Clerk at 815-334-4242 about property sold for back taxes.
